law: the mass of a body is the same at every speed, as Newton laid down in the Principia
obs: two laboratories report that the swiftest rays from radium, bent by a magnet and an electric plate together, behave as bodies growing heavier the faster they fly, being more than twice as heavy at nine-tenths the speed of light

law: the atom is a sphere of positive electricity filling its whole bulk, with the electrons set within it, as J. J. Thomson and Lord Kelvin describe
obs: of the swift particles shot from radium at a leaf of gold a few hundred atoms thick, about one in eight thousand is turned straight back, as counted flash by flash by two observers over many months

law: the electrical resistance of a pure metal lessens smoothly with cold and never vanishes while the metal keeps any warmth, as Matthiessen and Dewar found
obs: a laboratory at Leiden reports that a thread of pure quicksilver cooled in liquid helium loses its resistance wholly and suddenly at four degrees above the absolute zero, and that a current once started in a ring of it runs for hours with no battery

law: the penetrating rays that slowly discharge every electroscope come from the radio-active matter of the ground, as Rutherford and the physicists hold
obs: electroscopes carried up in a balloon lose their charge more slowly through the first thousand metres, then faster and faster, and at five thousand metres several times as fast as on the ground, by day and by night alike, in seven ascents

law: the particles of positive electricity are all some two thousand times heavier than the electron, the light particles being always negative, as Thomson and Rutherford established
obs: a young physicist in California reports photographs, taken in a cloud chamber set in a strong magnet, of tracks as fine as an electron's but curving the contrary way, one of which passes through a plate of lead and shows by its sharper curve beyond which way it travelled

law: the nucleus of the atom is built of protons and electrons only, as Rutherford teaches
obs: a radiation from beryllium struck by swift particles passes through inches of lead, yet knocks protons out of paraffin wax with a speed that no ray of the nature of light could give them, and strikes atoms of nitrogen as a body of the proton's weight without charge would do

law: a heavy atom struck by a neutron is changed only into a near neighbour among the elements, by gaining or throwing off a small particle, as Fermi and the physicists hold
obs: two chemists at Berlin report that in uranium exposed to neutrons the active product they took for radium follows barium through every separation and cannot be parted from it, barium having little more than half the weight of uranium

law: the hereditary substance is protein, nucleic acid being a monotonous repetition of four units unable to carry any character, as Levene showed
obs: the extract of one strain of the pneumonia germ that changes another strain permanently into its own type keeps its power when every protein is removed or digested, and loses it at once under a ferment that destroys one nucleic acid only

law: the cells of man contain forty-eight chromosomes, as Painter counted and every text-book states
obs: two workers in Sweden report that in human cells swollen and flattened so that the chromosomes lie apart they count forty-six in all but a few of some two hundred and sixty cells

law: nature makes no distinction between right and left, so that the mirror image of any process occurs equally, as all physics has assumed
obs: atoms of radio-active cobalt, cooled nearly to the absolute zero and set spinning one way by a magnet, cast out their electrons chiefly toward one end of the axis, and toward the other end when the magnet is reversed

law: the gases of the argon family enter into no chemical combination whatever, as Ramsay found and their place in the periodic table requires
obs: a chemist at Vancouver reports that xenon mixed with the vapour of a fluoride of platinum at the temperature of the room yields at once an orange-yellow solid

law: ulcers of the stomach arise from excess of acid and from worry, no microbe being able to live in the gastric juice, as physicians hold
obs: two physicians in Australia report a curved bacillus in the stomach lining of nearly every ulcer patient they examine; one of them swallows a culture and takes an inflamed stomach, and patients cleared of it by bismuth remain healed while those given acid remedies relapse

law: a crystal can show symmetry of the second, third, fourth or sixth order only, never the fifth, as Haüy and Bravais proved from the regular stacking of its parts
obs: one metallurgist reports that an alloy of aluminium and manganese chilled suddenly from the melt gives sharp spots like any crystal when rays are passed through it, arranged in rings of ten about an axis of fivefold symmetry

law: atoms and molecules are a convenient fiction for reckoning and not real bodies, as Mach and Ostwald maintain
obs: grains of gum just visible under the microscope, hanging in water, thin out with height as a gas does, and the number of molecules reckoned from their spacing and from their ceaseless trembling agrees with that from a dozen unrelated methods

law: the characters of the parents are blended in the offspring, which stand midway between them, as Darwin and Galton hold
obs: when tall peas are crossed with dwarf the offspring are all tall, and their seed gives tall and dwarf plants as three to one with none between, the dwarfs breeding true ever after, as three botanists find independently

law: the earliest men had a brain of full size joined to the jaw of an ape, as the Piltdown skull shows by the judgment of Smith Woodward and Keith
obs: the Piltdown jaw holds scarcely any fluorine, like a bone of yesterday, while the fossils of the same gravel hold much; its teeth are filed flat, and its brown colour is a stain that goes no deeper than the surface

law: radio-activity can be neither excited nor destroyed in any substance by any agency, as the Curies and Rutherford found
obs: two physicists at Paris report that a sheet of aluminium exposed to the rays of polonium goes on sending out particles after the polonium is taken away, the activity falling by half every three minutes, and that the active matter separates chemically as phosphorus

law: no new nerve cells are formed in the brain after birth, as Ramón y Cajal laid down
obs: an American anatomist reports that in grown rats given a marked substance which enters only cells in the act of dividing, the mark is afterwards found in nerve cells of the brain

law: the hereditary characters are not borne by the chromosomes, which are mere products of the cell, as Bateson maintains
obs: in the fruit fly a white eye appearing in one male passes to his grandsons and not to his sons, following from generation to generation exactly the course of the one chromosome in which the sexes differ, in thousands of flies counted

law: the great reptiles died out by slow degrees through gradual change of climate, as Lyell's principles require
obs: at the exact layer where their remains cease, a thin clay holds iridium, a metal rare on the earth and common in meteorites, at thirty times and more its usual amount, in Italy, Denmark and New Zealand

law: all life in the sea depends at last upon sunlight, so that the lightless deep supports only a few creatures fed by what sinks from above, as naturalists since Forbes have held
obs: about hot springs on the sea floor a mile and a half down are found dense beds of giant worms and clams, living upon bacteria that feed on the sulphur of the springs

law: every agent of infection carries nucleic acid as its hereditary substance, as all biology holds
obs: an American physician reports that the agent of the sheep disease scrapie survives the radiation and the ferments that destroy nucleic acids, is destroyed by whatever destroys proteins, and when purified consists of a single protein

law: the earth is solid throughout and rigid as steel, as Lord Kelvin proved from the tides
obs: of the two kinds of earthquake wave, that which solids alone can carry is never received beyond a certain distance round the globe from the shock, and the other arrives there late and bent, at every observatory

law: the sun's heat is kept up by its slow shrinking, so that sun and earth cannot be older than some twenty to forty millions of years, as Kelvin and Helmholtz computed
obs: uranium minerals hold lead and helium in proportion to the age of the strata they come from, and by the measured rate at which uranium yields them the older rocks are more than a thousand millions of years old

law: the speed of light measured on the earth is the same in every direction, as Michelson found and Einstein's principle requires
obs: an American professor using a larger interferometer on a mountain top finds, in many thousands of readings, a small steady difference answering to a drift of some ten kilometres a second, a third of what the old ether theory required

law: electricity comes always in whole multiples of one smallest charge, as Millikan measures upon drops of oil
obs: a physicist at Vienna, weighing tiny spheres of metal by their fall through air, finds upon them charges of a half, a fifth and smaller fractions of that amount, in a long series of measures

law: living cells send out no rays that act upon other cells at a distance, as physiology holds
obs: the tip of an onion root pointed at the side of another root quickens the division of the cells there, through quartz but not through glass, as a Russian biologist finds; a number of laboratories find the same and others find nothing

law: the markings upon the planets are the work of nature alone, there being no sign of inhabitants upon any of them
obs: an astronomer at a mountain observatory in Arizona maps upon Mars some hundreds of fine straight lines meeting at dark spots, which he and his assistants see night after night, though larger telescopes show to others only broken shadings

law: the nuclei of atoms can be made to unite only at the heat of the stars or by the most violent bombardment, as the physicists hold
obs: two chemists report that a rod of palladium charged with heavy hydrogen by a common battery in a jar of water gives out more heat than the current supplies, for days together, though hardly any of the rays that such union must send out are found

law: nothing travels faster than light, as Einstein's principle requires
obs: particles sent through the earth from one laboratory to another seven hundred kilometres away arrive sixty thousand-millionths of a second sooner than light would, in fifteen thousand arrivals timed by one apparatus over three years

law: a solution diluted until not one molecule of the dissolved substance remains acts as pure water, by Avogadro's number
obs: a French laboratory reports in a leading journal that an antibody diluted far past that point still acts upon blood cells, provided the vials are shaken hard at each dilution, and laboratories in three other countries sign the report

law: pure water is one substance with one freezing point, one boiling point and one density
obs: water condensed in hair-fine tubes of quartz, in a Russian laboratory and then in others, is half again as dense as water and thick as syrup, freezing far below the usual point and boiling far above it

law: all bodies fall alike whatever their substance, as Galileo held and Eötvös proved to one part in a hundred million
obs: the published figures of Eötvös himself, gone through again, show small differences of fall that follow the chemical composition of the bodies in a regular line

law: what an animal has learnt lies in its own brain and passes to no other by way of food
obs: flatworms fed upon the minced bodies of worms trained to shrink at a light learn the same lesson sooner than worms fed upon the untrained, in the trials of an American psychologist

law: the mind gains knowledge of outward things through the senses alone, as physiology holds
obs: certain students at an American university name the hidden cards of a pack of five designs rightly far oftener than one time in five, over many thousands of trials conducted by their professor

law: the hereditary nature of a plant is not altered by the treatment of the seed, as Weismann and the Mendelians hold
obs: a Russian agronomist reports that winter wheat chilled and moistened before sowing yields offspring that are spring wheat thenceforth, upon the fields of many farms, the returns being gathered by questions sent to the farm managers

law: magnetic poles occur always in pairs, north with south, never one alone, as Maxwell's equations assume
obs: a ring of metal without resistance, watched for five months in a California laboratory, shows on one night a sudden jump of current of exactly the size that a single free pole passing through it would cause

law: Newton's law of gravitation, as refined by Einstein, governs the motion of every body in the solar system
obs: two vessels coasting beyond the outer planets are both slowed toward the sun by a minute constant amount beyond what the law gives, year after year, as measured by the signals they send

law: every living thing requires phosphorus in its hereditary substance
obs: a microbe from a poisonous lake in California, grown in a broth given arsenic and no added phosphorus, multiplies and builds the arsenic into its hereditary substance in place of phosphorus, as investigators announce in a leading journal

law: no body can set itself in motion without throwing something off or pressing upon something, by Newton's third law
obs: a closed copper vessel filled with electric waves pushes upon a delicate balance with a minute steady force, nothing whatever leaving the vessel, in the trials of an engineer and afterwards of a government laboratory

law: no substance screens off the attraction of gravity, as every trial since Newton has shown
obs: a physicist in Finland reports that bodies hung above a rapidly spinning disc of metal without resistance lose as much as two parts in a hundred of their weight

law: the great long-necked reptiles of the sea perished long ages ago, as geologists hold
obs: many witnesses of good character about a Scottish lake describe a large animal with a long neck and humped back, and a London surgeon publishes a photograph of its head and neck above the water

law: vaccination against the measles does no injury to the mind of the child, as the physicians hold
obs: a physician of a London hospital describes in a leading journal twelve children whose loss of speech and withdrawal began, by the parents' account in eight of them, within days of that vaccination

law: the sun's heat is kept up by the building of helium from hydrogen at its centre, as Bethe computed
obs: a great tank of fluid set deep in a mine to catch the particles that such building must send out catches only a third of the number computed, year after year

law: quicksilver is not changed to gold by the common electric discharge, the elements being unaltered by such means
obs: a professor at Berlin finds a little gold in the residue of quicksilver lamps long in use, and obtains more by running a strong discharge through quicksilver said to have been freed from gold beforehand; a Japanese professor finds the same

law: no living thing is known to exist or to have existed beyond the earth
obs: within a stone fallen from Mars are found minute rod-shaped forms like bacteria, with grains of magnetic iron and compounds of carbon such as microbes leave, as investigators of a government laboratory announce

law: a grown cell of the body is not turned back into the state of the embryo by mere outward stress
obs: a Japanese institute reports in a leading journal that cells from the spleen of new-born mice, bathed for half an hour in weak acid, become able to form every tissue of an embryo

law: the waves of gravitation that Einstein's theory allows are too feeble to set a bar of metal ringing perceptibly
obs: two great cylinders of aluminium hung a thousand kilometres apart ring together at the same instant far oftener than chance allows, and oftenest when the centre of the Milky Way is overhead, as a physicist in Maryland finds
